key_insight: A next-token prediction model trained on multi-modal sleep signals can learn generalisable physiological representations that transfer well to downstream health tasks.
clinical_relevance: This approach could reduce the amount of labelled data needed for sleep staging and other physiology-based screening tasks, potentially improving scalability across clinical settings.
method: Trained Hypnos on 20,000+ overnight polysomnography recordings from eight sensing modalities including EEG, ECG, and respiratory signals.
Converted each modality into discrete token streams using residual vector quantization.
Used a large auto-regressive RQ-Transformer to predict the next token across modalities in parallel and generate embeddings for downstream use.
evidence_signal: Across multiple benchmarks, Hypnos outperformed existing foundation models, matched strong supervised sleep-stage baselines with 100x less labelled data, and surpassed a dedicated ECG foundation model for atrial fibrillation detection.
watch_item: Performance was shown in benchmark settings, so real-world deployment will still need external validation across diverse patient populations, devices, and clinical workflows.
paper_title: Next-Token Prediction Learns Generalisable Representations of Sleep Physiology
